AWSModule.initialize binds the STSClient.send result to te and tests its UserId, Account and Arn fields (s1; f1:2).
All three identity fields must be truthy for initialize to return true, and isValid positively gates getAllSecretValues without a negation (s1, s2; f1:2).
The tested identity fields come from the awaited STS GetCallerIdentity response, fitting server_response (s1).
The auth object is constructed from the bundled GoogleAuth export, and initialize tests the awaited getProjectId result through t (s3, s16; f1:2).
The getProjectId result must be truthy in t&&r before isValidCredentials becomes true; isValid positively gates secret collection (s3, s16, s4).
The project identifier identifies the cloud project whose secrets are enumerated, so target_artifact fits the tested project context (s3; f1:2).
The authenticated-token, platform, token-prefix and user checks enable the extraction and migration calls in the nested then block (s5, s6, s7).
The checks activate extraction and migration for usable GitHub credentials on Linux or macOS; they do not test for an analysis environment (s5, s6).
The combined checks target authenticated GitHub accounts with supported token prefixes on the selected operating systems before extraction and migration (s5, s6).

Both nested then guards contain s7, whose extraction and migration calls resolve to methods on the GitHubModule instance created in main. Those definitions contain the cited write and spawn sinks (s9, s10, s13, s14; f1:2).

The only calls to extraction and migration in the bundle are s9 and s13 inside both guards. The class export is internal to the bundle, and the entry point exposes no alternate caller or instance (f1:2).

The resolved fs and child_process modules provide the file write and spawn sinks; the extraction script uploads a persistent push-triggered workflow. The migration script clones private or internal repositories, pushes copies and makes them public, supporting exfiltration (s8, s11, s12; f1:2).

isValid returns initialize, whose successful path requires the identity response fields and whose cached success is set on that same path. Thus the single c93 condition enables the right-hand secret collection region, with minimum one condition (s1, s2, s15; f1:2).
A valid STS identity enables getAllSecretValues; the failed-validation path leaves the collected secrets empty (s1, s2, s15).
Successful identity validation activates secret collection rather than avoiding an analysis environment (s1, s2).
Identity validation establishes usable AWS credentials before Secrets Manager enumeration and secret reads, fitting data_availability (s1, s2; f1:2).

initialize sets isValidCredentials only when both the project identifier and client are truthy, and isValid returns that flag. The conjunction therefore controls s17 and requires both conditions (s3, s16, s4, s17).
Successful project and client discovery enables getAllSecretValues; failed validation leaves the secret list empty (s3, s16, s4, s17).
The checks activate secret collection for an available project and authenticated client, with no analysis-environment avoidance (s3, s16, s4).
Project and client discovery establishes the context and credentials needed to list secrets and access their versions, fitting data_availability (s3, s16, s4; f1:2).
The getAllSecretValues call is directly inside the right-hand assignment region of the positive isValid short circuit, so no intervening witness hops are needed (s4, s17, s18).

The only invocation of the GCP getAllSecretValues method in the bundle is s18 on the then side of s4. The GCPModule export stays internal to the bundle and no alternate caller, timer or exposed instance reaches this call (f1:2).
